tasks.short: Recommend shipping options that reduce cost or environmental impact.

steps.what: Verify shipment constraints, customer priorities and actual carrier offers
Compare explicit total prices and consistently scoped environmental estimates
Choose feasible solutions and judge cost, service and environmental tradeoffs
Write and approve the complete recommendation, assumptions and customer recipient
Save the approved final shipping recommendation
Send the approved final shipping recommendation to the customer

tasks.design: Use native forwarding comparisons in {OPS_SYSTEM} and an existing deterministic emissions calculator ({OTHER}) to compare checked actual offers. Keep feasibility, tradeoff judgement and writing full time. Save and customer send each follow approval of the completed recommendation. No capacity is booked or reduction guaranteed.
tasks.previous_blocker: A low price and a low emissions estimate may describe incompatible service assumptions.
tasks.enabler_now: Explicit offers can be compared under one declared calculation scope.
tasks.still_hard: Service reliability, uncertain factors and customer tradeoffs require judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Explain a practical option and its limitations without overstating environmental benefits.
tasks.altitude: Transparent comparison supports human shipping advice.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: freight calculators can compare explicit prices and estimated emissions under a stated common methodology.

assumptions: Shares are provisional. Establish actual current comparison and transfer work; current calculator use earns no new saving. No emissions reduction baseline is invented.

Customer supplies cargo, origin, destination, dates and priorities; carriers supply actual routes, prices and service terms. s1 agent captures/checks quantity, weight, units, route legs, modes, equipment, offer expiry and charge components at full time. The existing approved calculator supplies documented factors and versioned methodology; missing parameters remain qualified estimates or require manual comparison.

s2 performs explicit arithmetic, not invented reliability scoring. s3 tests feasibility. s4 writes/checks final recommendation, limitations, sources and recipient at full time. Native views/calculators precede code.
a1 and a2 each bind the completed s4 version and their own destination; changes revoke approval. This is advice, with no carrier commitment.
research_questions: What comparison work remains once current native price and emissions outputs use consistent assumptions?

incremental.description: Verify comparison fields and emissions method updates

approvals.approved_version: s4 complete recommendation and shipment reference
s4 complete recommendation and customer recipient

Low assumes partial coverage. Actual evidence capture, credibility assessment, selection, written recommendations, filing and sends retain full effort.

tasks.short: Review freight carriers environmental records for shipping decisions.

steps.what: Obtain carrier environmental records and inspect their scope, date and provenance
inputs: actual carrier environmental reports and supporting records

steps.what: Capture source metrics, units, periods, assurance claims and exclusions with page references
Convert compatible units and display explicitly comparable carrier metrics beside source references
Assess credibility, incompatible scopes and relevance to the shipment decision
Write and approve the carrier review and its shipping-decision limitations
Commit the approved carrier review to the supplier record

tasks.design: Use a checked spreadsheet comparison in {SPREADSHEET} to convert only compatible units and lay out captured source metrics. Keep reading, provenance checks, scope interpretation and the written review fully human. Commit the complete approved review separately to {OPS_SYSTEM}; no model scores corporate credibility or chooses carriers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Corporate totals, intensity measures and assurance claims can cover different activities.
tasks.enabler_now: Explicit source fields allow deterministic unit handling without treating unlike measures as comparable.
tasks.still_hard: Credibility and relevance to the actual shipment depend on reading the source limitations.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise that a broad corporate claim does not establish performance on a specific service.
tasks.altitude: Less comparison formatting; unchanged source criticism.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: spreadsheets can convert compatible units and present captured environmental metrics with explicit scope and source columns.

assumptions: Shares are provisional. Verify actual repeated unit/layout work and supplier-record posting; existing templates earn no new benefit.

Carrier is the producer of reports and claimed assurance documents; no claim is treated as verified merely because it is published. s1 reads/checks provenance; s2 agent captures metric_name, value, unit, period, boundary, mode coverage, assurance wording, exclusions and page reference at full time.

s3 copies explicit fields and converts documented compatible units. Incompatible scopes are displayed separately, not normalised by guessed load or distance. s4 retains credibility and shipment relevance decisions; unsupported information stays unknown.

s5 writes/checks the complete review at full time before a1 binds its version and supplier destination. No external circulation or procurement decision is silently added. Use existing spreadsheet and supplier-record functions before custom code.
research_questions: Which carrier metrics are truly comparable once their periods and operating scopes are read?

incremental.description: Check unit conversion mappings and source-field definitions

approvals.approved_version: s5 final carrier review and supplier record

tasks.short: Analyze shipping routes for lower environmental impact.

steps.what: Verify feasible route alternatives and inspect available environmental input evidence
Capture route legs, mode, distance basis, load and declared calculation assumptions
Calculate route scenarios consistently and present sensitivity to declared uncertain inputs
Interpret scenario limitations and test whether lower-impact alternatives remain operationally feasible
Write and approve the final route analysis with assumptions and caveats
File the approved route analysis and its input-version references

tasks.design: Use an existing deterministic route-emissions calculator ({OTHER}) to run explicitly captured feasible scenarios with a declared common scope. The forwarder owns evidence gathering, field capture, assumption selection, operational interpretation and report writing. The finished analysis is approved before filing; no route is booked or live shipment changed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Route comparisons change when missing load and distance assumptions are silently filled.
tasks.enabler_now: A versioned calculator can repeat the same declared method across explicit scenarios.
tasks.still_hard: Actual service constraints and uncertain environmental inputs limit confident ranking.
tasks.human_edge: Explain when an apparent improvement depends on an assumption that operations cannot support.
tasks.altitude: Repeatable scenario arithmetic supports human environmental route analysis.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: deterministic transport calculators can repeat environmental calculations for route scenarios using a declared common methodology.

assumptions: Shares are provisional. Establish actual manual scenario calculation and filing effort; an already-used calculator earns no new saving. No local emissions baseline or measured reduction is claimed.

Customer provides shipment needs and carrier provides actual service alternatives. s1 checks these sources; s2 forwarder records origin/destination by leg, mode, distance basis, shipment weight, equipment, load assumption, method/version and explicitly chosen sensitivity values at full time. Documented calculator method supplies factors; unknown actual loads remain declared assumptions, not invented observations.

s3 performs arithmetic on those explicit scenarios. Missing or incompatible inputs require manual analysis with no claimed s3 benefit. s4 retains feasibility and interpretation; no model ranks unverified environmental claims.
s5 writes/checks final analysis, limitations and source versions before a1. Edits revoke approval. Existing calculator and document filing features precede code; no external send is performed.
research_questions: How sensitive is the preferred feasible route to the declared uncertain load and distance inputs?

incremental.description: Verify calculator method versions and scenario mappings

approvals.approved_version: s5 final analysis and source-version references

tasks.short: Consider environmental sustainability when choosing merchandise packing methods.

steps.what: Inspect merchandise protection needs and destination packing restrictions
inputs: actual merchandise and shipment handling needs

steps.what: Inspect candidate packing materials and evidence for protection, reuse and disposal claims
inputs: available packing samples and supplier specifications

steps.what: Record candidate material quantities, weights, dimensions and supported reuse or disposal conditions
Compare explicit material totals, packed volume and supported end-of-use conditions
Select packing that balances protection, restrictions and supported environmental considerations
Write and approve the final packing method and evidence limitations
Commit the approved packing method record

tasks.design: Use a native spreadsheet comparison of captured material quantities, packed volume and supported reuse/disposal conditions. Keep merchandise inspection, candidate inspection, source interpretation and protective packing choice fully human. Write/check the selected method before a separate {OPS_SYSTEM} record commit. No invented sustainability score or automatic substitution of protective material.
tasks.previous_blocker: Less material can increase damage, and a recycling claim may not apply at the destination.
tasks.enabler_now: Explicit material and volume arithmetic can make candidate tradeoffs easier to inspect.
tasks.still_hard: Protection, actual destination recovery options and credible material evidence require judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Avoid reducing packaging in a way that damages goods or creates an unsupported environmental claim.
tasks.altitude: Less material comparison work with retained physical and environmental judgement.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a spreadsheet can total captured packing material quantities and volumes while preserving source-qualified reuse and disposal conditions.

assumptions: Shares are provisional. Verify actual manual material comparison and posting; an existing packing calculator earns no new saving. No damage or environmental reduction baseline is invented.

Agent observes merchandise and packing samples in s1/s2; supplier supplies specifications and source claims, and actual destination sources support stated recovery conditions. s3 agent captures candidate_id, material_type, quantity, unit_weight, packed_dimensions, source_reference and explicitly supported reuse/disposal conditions at full time. Missing conditions stay unknown rather than assumed recyclable everywhere.

s4 totals explicit weights/volumes and lays out supported conditions; it creates no lifecycle impact score or protective performance conclusion. s5 retains safety/protection and restriction judgement. Physical inspection is not shortened.

s6 writes/checks final method and limitations before a1 binds the completed version. This decision record does not place a material order, assign packers or silently send instructions. Native spreadsheet and shipment-record features precede code.
research_questions: Which feasible protective packing candidates have supported differences in material use and destination recovery conditions?

incremental.description: Maintain material units and source-condition fields

approvals.approved_version: s6 final packing method, limitations and shipment reference
